capability.description: Research, frame, generate, compare, and review high-quality product marketing case studies and presentations without building a new general-purpose website generator.
constraints: Human owner remains final authority on taste and promotion.
Native HTML/CSS/JS remains a fast control renderer.
Product claims must remain grounded in primary sources.
External research may support market pain but cannot become product efficacy proof.
Candidate designs must remain materially different rather than collapse into one template.
At least one Three.js/WebGL direction should be available when spatial interaction helps explain the product.
non_goals: Build a hosted no-code website builder.
Replace mature visual editors or design-system tools.
Create an automated aesthetic winner score.
Require one framework or renderer for every marketing artifact.

searches.surface: Owner repository inventory and existing Design Bakery case studies
searches.query: existing marketing case study HTML presentation evidence workflows and reusable deployment surface

receipts.note: Existing production host and native HTML case-study surface already used successfully for FOSSIL and Study OS.

searches.query: open source AI design workflow case study generator brand as code visual editor website builder Three.js

receipts.note: Agent-native design skills and DESIGN.md workflow.
Agent skill suite covering insights, positioning, content, design, QA, and launch.
Open-source brand case-study generator with model-directed art direction.
Brand identity as code with reusable token outputs.
Open-source visual editing workflow for code-backed sites.
Mature WebGL/3D rendering library for immersive candidate variants.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong fit for rapidly generated expressive static case studies, presentations, and gallery pages.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Already owned and deployed by the project owner.
tradeoffs.license: Internal ownership; no new external license dependency for authored page code.
tradeoffs.security: Static public artifact surface with no new privileged runtime required for the experiment.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Can host plain HTML, CSS, JS, SVG, canvas, and external module-enhanced variants.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Low because routing and deployment already exist.
tradeoffs.performance: Static pages are lightweight by default and can be tuned per candidate.
material_reasons: Recent Study OS and FOSSIL work demonstrates strong output quality with this path.
It provides the comparison control against which OSS-assisted approaches should be judged.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong fit for design briefs, visual-direction discipline, frontend craft, and anti-generic-AI design guidance.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Active public project at research time; exact release should be rechecked before installation.
tradeoffs.license: Upstream licenses vary by bundled skill; verify before copying code or assets.
tradeoffs.security: Use as a local/reference workflow; no need to make it a production runtime dependency.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Skill-oriented structure can inform or be invoked by compatible agent environments.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Low to moderate depending on whether it is installed or only used as a workflow reference.
tradeoffs.performance: Not on the deployed page runtime when used only for design guidance.
material_reasons: Its frontend-design workflow explicitly starts from audience, job, domain, and emotional tone.
It is useful upstream of HTML generation rather than replacing Design Bakery deployment.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong end-to-end agent workflow precedent from insights and positioning through design, QA, and launch.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Active public project at research time.
tradeoffs.license: Verify repository and third-party license files before code reuse.
tradeoffs.security: No production dependency is required if used as a process/reference adapter.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Plain skill files make the workflow portable across several coding agents.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Low as a process reference; higher if adopting its Astro/Cloudflare production stack, which is not required here.
tradeoffs.performance: Not relevant to deployed candidates unless its generated stack is adopted.
material_reasons: Its fixed production stack is unnecessary for Design Bakery, so reuse should focus on process rather than hosting.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong reference for committing to a specific case-study aesthetic and planning a sequence of visual frames.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Public project; exact current state should be checked before execution.
tradeoffs.license: Verify upstream license before reusing implementation or templates.
tradeoffs.security: Keep out of the deployed runtime unless intentionally adopted.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Useful specifically in the downstream art-direction phase after positioning exists.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Moderate if executed, low if used only as a comparative art-direction reference.
tradeoffs.performance: Not relevant to static candidate runtime when used as a planning adapter.
material_reasons: It preserves model art-direction freedom rather than reducing the output to one rigid page template.
It starts later than Fluffy System's market/audience research, so it is complementary rather than full coverage.

tradeoffs.fitness: Useful after a brand direction is chosen and needs a durable token/voice contract.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Newer public project; maturity should be rechecked before depending on its schema.
tradeoffs.license: Verify upstream license before implementation reuse.
tradeoffs.security: Brand contract tooling need not be part of the deployed site runtime.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Can export brand definitions to several implementation formats.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Low for an optional export/adaptation layer.
tradeoffs.performance: No runtime cost when used only at build/design time.
material_reasons: Useful for preserving an approved brand after human selection.
Not a substitute for the market research and creative-direction decision itself.

tradeoffs.fitness: Potentially useful for visual iteration after a code-backed candidate exists.
tradeoffs.maintenance: Popular public project; exact current capabilities should be checked before use.
tradeoffs.license: Verify upstream licensing before local deployment or code reuse.
tradeoffs.security: Treat as an optional editor, not a required production dependency.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Useful downstream for visual code edits rather than upstream positioning research.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Moderate because the current Design Bakery control path is already direct and fast.
tradeoffs.performance: No deployed runtime cost if used only as an editor.
material_reasons: Could improve iterative visual tuning after owner feedback.
Does not replace native generation or upstream research.

tradeoffs.fitness: Strong fit for experimental candidates where spatial structure, transformation, or simulation communicates the product mechanism.
tradeoffs.license: MIT upstream at research time; pin and recheck the exact version used in a deployed candidate.
tradeoffs.security: Client-side rendering library; external CDN imports should fail soft and may later be vendored if selected.
tradeoffs.extensibility: Broad 3D/WebGL ecosystem with optional React integrations.
tradeoffs.integration_cost: Low for isolated static-page experiments, higher for production-grade interactive applications.
tradeoffs.performance: Requires explicit mobile, reduced-motion, and fallback discipline.
material_reasons: Provides the requested immersive aesthetic comparison.
Should remain an optional renderer rather than force the whole marketing system into a JS app architecture.

probes.rationale: Initial experiment can reuse documented workflow ideas without installing another runtime; execution can be added if the gallery indicates a meaningful value hypothesis.
Its Astro/Cloudflare production stack is unnecessary for the current Design Bakery deployment; process comparison is sufficient for the first gallery.
Use its art-direction pattern as a comparison reference first; execute later only if a Casa-specific output is valuable.
BrandSpec becomes more useful after a winning brand direction exists.
Onlook is primarily an iteration surface; use it after owner feedback if direct edits become slower than visual editing.

evidence: Design Bakery hidden gallery Three.js candidates

decision.rationale: Do not build a new general-purpose marketing renderer. Preserve the research/storytelling process in Fluffy System, reuse Design Bakery for output, use mature OSS selectively for design/art-direction/brand/editing patterns, and use Three.js only as an optional immersive renderer.
residual_uncertainty: The first gallery may show that one external design workflow produces a repeatable quality improvement worth deeper integration.
Some tools may be more useful after human selection than during first-pass generation.
reconsideration_triggers: Native HTML generation becomes a repeated bottleneck rather than a strength.
An OSS tool consistently produces substantially better owner-rated outputs across multiple subjects.
Maintaining brand consistency across many selected projects becomes more expensive than adopting a brand-as-code contract.

human_review.evidence: Owner instruction on 2026-09-08: prefer reuse over building unnecessary systems; owner will judge final rendered candidates.
